fitAnalysis.assessment:
This is a weak fit at 38%: your backend engineering skills are strong, but the role's core search and vector database requirements are missing from your profile.

**Strengths:**
- Java experience with demonstrated performance optimization (p99 latency cut from 480 ms to 120 ms)
- PostgreSQL and distributed systems experience across fintech at senior level
- Code review and cross-functional leadership across a 9-month migration

**Gaps:**
- No Elasticsearch, Lucene, or search relevance experience (the role's core domain)
- No vector database knowledge: HNSW or IVF algorithms absent from your profile
- No Solr, MongoDB, or Cassandra exposure for the preferred storage breadth

**Recommendation:** Before applying, complete Elastic's free Elasticsearch Engineer training and build a small personal project using Elasticsearch vector search to create concrete, claimable evidence for the role's must-have requirements.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Elastic

Dear Hiring Manager,

Building search and retrieval systems at scale means solving the same problem that consumed much of my work at Lumen Payments: keeping reads fast under high, unpredictable load. When our payment status API slowed under pressure, I moved hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis and brought p99 latency down sharply. That instinct for diagnosing where a system breaks and redesigning around the constraint is what I'd bring to Elasticsearch's Search Relevance team.

As a Senior Software Engineer working in Java and Kotlin with Spring Boot, I've spent eleven years building services that handle large, continuous event volumes on Kafka, designing APIs, and reviewing code across distributed teams. I led a migration from a monolith to six independent services, coordinating four engineers over nine months while keeping the payments platform live. I'm also comfortable with the asynchronous, written-first collaboration that Elastic's globally distributed team runs on: my incident post-mortems and design documents were the primary coordination tool across time zones. On the data storage side, I have hands-on production experience with PostgreSQL and Redis, and I've contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library, so the pull-request workflow your team uses every day is familiar ground. I don't yet have direct Elasticsearch or Lucene experience, and I'll say that plainly; what I do have is a strong Java foundation, a track record of learning new systems quickly under production pressure, and the kind of low-level curiosity about why data structures behave the way they do that your role description calls for.

I'd welcome a conversation about how my background fits the Search Relevance team's work. I'm available at your convenience.

Kind regards,
Priya Raman

applicationEmail.subject: Application: Senior Software Engineer - Search, Priya Raman
applicationEmail.body:
Hi there,

Building high-performance, low-latency systems in Java is work I know well: at Lumen Payments I cut p99 latency on a payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by rethinking how hot reads were served, and I designed a settlement service handling around 40 million events a day on Kafka. That kind of work, finding where a system slows down and fixing it at the data-structure or architecture level, is what draws me to the search engine engineering Elastic is doing. My CV and cover letter are attached with more detail on my background. I'm available to start conversations immediately and can interview any time that suits your team.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
